Article Title: Google rolls out new Gemini tools to help small businesses save time
Article Text:
Brand-consistent visuals

Financial insights from messy records

Business owners in India and elsewhere

Availability

Google has announced a set of new Gemini tools aimed at small business owners, led by a dedicated business landing page inside the Gemini app. The company says tens of millions of small business owners already use Gemini to brainstorm products, handle customer feedback and analyse performance, and that the new tools are meant to give them time back so they can focus on the work they started their companies for. The announcement was published on Google’s India blog by Vishnu Sivaji, Senior Director of the Gemini app.The landing page is designed as a central hub where owners can build their brand, analyse finances and understand customer insights. Gemini can also now connect to Google Business Profile, Google Ads and Google Workspace, as well as third-party apps including Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero.Businesses can now define their brand style in Gemini by uploading a website, brand kit, fonts or colour palettes. Paired with Nano Banana 2.1, Google’s latest image-generation model, Gemini can produce end-to-end visuals for product launches and marketing campaigns. Google says Gemini remembers the brand style, so owners do not have to upload their guidelines each time they want new on-brand material.Gemini can also turn disorganised spreadsheets, receipts and purchase records into clear financial graphics and interactive models within seconds, according to Google.The aim is to let owners get insights in plain language rather than working through the numbers themselves.Google highlighted several users to illustrate the tools. In Maharashtra, farmer and content creator Santosh Jadhav turned his traditional fields into a ginger farm with no formal training or local mentors. He used Gemini as a virtual agronomist to judge soil suitability, calculate seed requirements and draft an investment budget, and he shares his farming journey online to show how easily AI can be used in everyday agriculture.In Jakarta, Gumilang turned a neglected space under train tracks into Barelz Arena, a sports and entertainment hub. With no background in branding or sports, he used Gemini to develop a “Brazilian-street” visual identity, design merchandise and draft partnership proposals. In Bordeaux, France, ceramicist Morgane says Gemini saves her two to three hours a day by drafting product descriptions, newsletters and social media hooks. In Goiânia, Brazil, personal organiser Patricia Morais uses Gemini for customer service and content while working on accessible products such as clothing QR codes for people with visual impairments.The business landing page, the new marketing and finance skills and the additional connected apps will begin rolling out in the coming days to all Gemini app users worldwide, Google said. For larger organisations that want centralised admin controls, data governance and enterprise-grade security, the company pointed to its separate Gemini for business offering.
Article Summary: Gemini now has a dedicated business landing page for small business owners. Businesses can define their brand style in Gemini by uploading a website, brand kit, fonts or colour palettes. Google says Gemini remembers the brand style, so owners do not have to upload their guidelines each time they want new on-brand material.

Article Title: Microsoft expands sovereign cloud tools to give businesses greater control over data and AI
Article Text:
Here’s the full blog post shared by Microsoft’s Douglas Phillips

Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates expand its Microsoft Sovereign Cloud offering, allowing organisations to choose how and where sensitive data and applications are managed, including in environments that can operate without an internet connection. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally. Microsoft said the move is designed to help organisations meet regional regulations, strengthen security and keep critical services running during disruptions, while continuing to use cloud and AI technology."This challenge is becoming more important as advanced cloud and AI capabilities move into public services, regulated processes and essential operations. Organizations are considering more than where data resides. They also seek to understand who can access and operate their systems, how sensitive digital assets remain protected, which technology dependencies matter most and whether critical services can continue as regulatory, geopolitical, security or network conditions change.Digital sovereignty should give organizations greater control and security over the technology they depend on, while continuing to innovate.Last year, we introduced Microsoft Sovereign Cloud to give customers more choice in how they address these requirements. Since then, we have continued to turn our commitments into practical capabilities across public cloud and customer-operated environments, while expanding how we enable partners to address sovereignty requirements in their local markets. Today, we are sharing the next stage of that work.A continuum of control, built around the workloadMicrosoft Sovereign Cloud diagram showing a continuum of sovereignty solutions across three areas: Sovereign Public Cloud for control, data protection and regional requirements; Sovereign Private Cloud for critical workloads across connected and disconnected environments; and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem for trusted, locally operated and specialized solutions.Our approach to digital sovereignty starts with the workload. Each workload carries different requirements for data, operations, technology dependencies, continuity and risk. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed to make it easier for organizations to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload without forcing every application into the same deployment model.Those needs can vary widely across organizations. A public-facing digital service may benefit from the scale and pace of innovation in the public cloud. A system supporting essential operations may need to continue running locally if connectivity is disrupted. An AI workload handling highly sensitive data may require models, data and processing to remain within a customer-controlled environment.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed around this workload-based approach, providing a continuum of management, control and options across Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem. Organizations can apply the level of control appropriate to each workload while maintaining a consistent approach to governance and operations across their digital estate. Sovereign Public Cloud adds capabilities for workloads that require greater control and transparency while continuing to benefit from the scale and innovation of Azure.Sovereign Private Cloud extends cloud capabilities into customer-operated environments, including connected and disconnected operations. The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the continuum through independently operated environments, specialized partners, locally relevant expertise and technologies that support customers’ sovereignty requirements.These are not isolated destinations. Customers can combine public cloud, private cloud and partner capabilities across their digital estate, applying different levels of control to different workloads as their operating needs evolve.Making control more visible in Sovereign Public CloudFor many workloads, the public cloud provides a combination of scale, innovation, integrated security and compliance. Organizations can benefit from these capabilities while applying additional sovereignty controls for residency, confidentiality, operator access, policy and continuity. Our work in Sovereign Public Cloud makes these controls easier to understand, apply and demonstrate.Sovereign Control Panel, entering public preview at Microsoft Ignite, brings these signals together in a unified Azure portal experience. It helps organizations understand their sovereignty posture, apply and manage controls, identify gaps and risks and take action to address them. It also supports business continuity readiness by helping customers understand workload dependencies and assess portability across operating environments when required.This visibility complements controls across the operator-access lifecycle. Just-in-time Access and Customer Lockbox give customers additional control over access to their environments. For customers in the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), we are rolling out Data Guardian, which adds European-resident oversight by a trusted EU partner for qualifying Microsoft engineer remote access to in-scope production systems. Production Touch Ledger, also launched with phased rollout in the EU and EFTA, creates tamper-evident records of that access and the actions performed.Azure Key Vault Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) already gives customers dedicated, single-tenant protection and control over the encryption keys used by supported Azure services. Last year, we committed to extending that control beyond Microsoft infrastructure. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, allowing customers to keep the root encryption key in hardware they own and operate on-premises or through a trusted third party. This gives organizations another option for workloads that require physical control of key hardware outside Microsoft infrastructure.Azure confidential computing helps protect supported data while it is processed in a hardware-based and attested trusted execution environment. We are also increasing transparency into the technologies that underpin that trust. Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, now in limited preview, applies confidential computing to approved multiparty collaboration, allowing participants to analyze shared sensitive data while limiting broader exposure of the underlying information.Together, these capabilities provide additional technical and operational controls that can support a broader digital sovereignty strategy aligned to an organization’s legal, policy, security, resilience and business requirements.Designing for resilience and operational independenceFor some workloads, digital sovereignty also means maintaining critical operations as connectivity, geopolitical and operating conditions change. Resilience must be designed from the start so essential workloads can continue operating through disruption.To help customers prepare for these scenarios, we are publishing new sovereign business continuity guidance and architecture patterns. These resources help organizations translate resilience requirements into architectures they can plan, implement and test before they are needed.For many workloads, the scale and geographic reach of the public cloud provide a strong foundation for resilience across locations and operating conditions. For workloads that require greater operational independence, Sovereign Private Cloud extends that continuum into customer-operated environments. It supports connected and disconnected operating models. The ability to transition workloads from connected to disconnected operations is entering public preview, giving organizations greater flexibility to sustain critical services as connectivity and operating requirements change.Bringing more of the application lifecycle under local controlOperational independence requires more than infrastructure. Increasingly, organizations need data, development tools, model capabilities and productivity services their applications depend on to operate within the same customer-controlled environment.Sovereign Private Cloud, built on Azure Local, extends Microsoft cloud capabilities into environments that customers operate and control. SQL Server on Azure Local is already generally available for connected and disconnected deployments. DocumentDB and Blob Storage on Azure Local are both entering public preview, giving organizations more choice in how they run and manage critical data within customer-controlled environments.GitHub Enterprise Local will become generally available at Microsoft Ignite as a validated GitHub Enterprise Server appliance on Azure Local, helping organizations keep repositories, code and development artifacts under local control. Developers can also use GitHub Copilot with locally hosted models for inference, bringing AI-assisted development closer to their code and data within the environments they control.The local application environment is expanding with Foundry Local. At Ignite, Foundry Local will become generally available for connected and disconnected operations on Azure Local, with an expanded model catalog that includes Microsoft, partner, open-weight and open-source models. Local inference and agentic retrieval will also enable users to interact with local enterprise data using natural language and receive responses grounded in that data. Integration with Microsoft 365 Local, available in preview for approved customers, extends this functionality to locally operated Microsoft SharePoint and Exchange servers.Confidential virtual machines on Azure Local are generally available, extending confidential computing capabilities to customer-controlled infrastructure. Hardware-encrypted memory and hardware-based isolation help protect sensitive data while it is being processed. Workload attestation adds assurance before sensitive data or keys are released. For regulated, sensitive and mission-critical workloads, these safeguards provide another layer of protection while giving organizations greater control over where their data and applications run.Azure Local will support multitenancy, allowing organizations to separate resources, governance and management across multiple tenants while sharing the underlying infrastructure. This significantly expands what customers with distinct business units or security boundaries can achieve with Sovereign Private Cloud. Multitenancy also creates new opportunities for local operators and service providers to deliver differentiated sovereign cloud services on Azure Local infrastructure.These additions bring more of the application lifecycle under local control, spanning data, development, productivity, AI and operations. Organizations can determine what runs locally based on the requirements of each workload.Extending the continuum through partnersGraphic titled "Sovereign Partner Ecosystem" with the subtitle "National clouds · Software · Services · Platform co-innovation," showing 32 partner logos: Accenture, AMD, Armada, Avanade, base-it, Bleu, Capgemini, Cirrus Data, CloudCasa by Catalogic, Cronos Groep, cTelecoms, DataON, Delos Cloud, Dell Technologies, F5, Felo, Fortinet, HPE, Inspark, Intel, Lenovo, Mattermost, Mistral, NVIDIA, Qualidev, Qumulo, RiverMeadow, Rubrik, Supermicro, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Veeam and WSO2.Navigating sovereignty is increasingly complex. Regulatory, security, operational and business requirements vary across countries, industries and workloads. Organizations must translate these needs into technology and operating models that work in their local context. Meeting these needs often requires a combination of technology, local operating authority, sector expertise and specialized solutions.The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the ways customers can address these requirements. National Partner Clouds, including Bleu Cloud in France and Delos Cloud in Germany, provide independently operated environments for customers that require a different ownership and operating model. Software partners can enhance Azure Local environments with capabilities across security, identity, observability, backup and recovery, migration, data, networking and applications. Digital sovereignty specialized partners combine Microsoft technologies with local knowledge and implementation expertise. Platform co-innovation partners expand infrastructure choice from datacenter to the edge.This ecosystem gives customers the flexibility to combine technology, operating models and trusted expertise based on the requirements of each workload.The next chapter of digital sovereigntyAI is amplifying both the opportunity and the impact of technology choices. As AI systems and agents interact with sensitive data, business processes and essential infrastructure, they also expand the security considerations organizations need to manage. Organizations need clear control over where these systems run, who can operate them, what actions they can take and how critical services continue when conditions change.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud brings these choices together as a continuum of control across the public cloud, customer-operated environments and our partner ecosystem. It gives organizations the flexibility to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload while continuing to benefit from cloud capabilities and ongoing innovation.We will continue to expand this continuum so organizations can innovate with cloud and AI while maintaining the control, confidentiality, resilience and operational authority their most important workloads require."
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally.

Article Title: Chennai Metrowater desilts 227 streets
Article Text:
Chennai:





Metrowater desilted 9.6km of sewer lines and 433 manholes using 218 machines across 227 streets in Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) limits on Monday. Metrowater monitors sewage pumping levels round-the-clock through an IoT-based system. After rainfall, if pumping levels drop, officials identify the affected stretch and deploy workers to clear blocks. It has deployed 29 sewage suction vehicles hired from other districts in addition to its existing fleet of 580 machines and 173 contract-operated jetting-cum-grabbing vehicles. Further, generators and fuel are kept ready to ensure uninterrupted operations at eight water treatment plants, 143 water distribution stations, 22 sewage treatment plants and 438 sewage pumping stations. Metrowater has also doubled daily drinking water quality testing from 900 to 1,800 samples across GCC’s 15 zones. Residents can report water supply and sewage complaints on the 1916 helpline.
Article Summary: Metrowater desilted 9.6km of sewer lines and 433 manholes using 218 machines across 227 streets in Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) limits on Monday. It has deployed 29 sewage suction vehicles hired from other districts in addition to its existing fleet of 580 machines.

Article Title: An Australian designer develops hempcrete tiles to recreate tree hollows and rocky crevices; shelters aim to help threatened wildlife, including eastern quolls and ringtail possums
Article Text:
How hempcrete tiles recreate tree hollows and rocky crevices

Why Australia's wildlife needs alternative shelters

Which animals could benefit from Bush Cradle?

Eastern quolls

Ringtail possums

Other native wildlife

Early field observations offer an encouraging sign

Who developed Bush Cradle?

What comes next for the project?

Australian designer Xavier Earls has developed Bush Cradle, a modular wildlife habitat system made from hempcrete tiles that mimic natural shelters such as tree hollows, fallen logs and rocky crevices. The system is designed to help conservationists create customised refuges for native animals facing habitat loss. Its four interlocking tile designs can be assembled into different configurations, including tree hollows and ground dens, with entrances tailored to individual species. The project aims to address the shortage of natural shelter for wildlife, including eastern quolls and ringtail possums. In an encouraging early observation, ringtail possums reportedly used a prototype overnight, offering an initial indication of the design's potential.Bush Cradle uses four tile shapes connected through a slot-and-pin mechanism, allowing shelters to be assembled, dismantled and rearranged by hand without conventional tools. This makes it possible to adapt their configurations to different species and environments.The tiles are made from fibrous hempcrete, chosen for its insulating properties. Their manufacture combines 3D printing and casting, with lightweight printed frames placed inside moulds before hempcrete is poured in and left to cure.Laser-cut wooden entrance pieces allow openings to be customised for different animals.According to Earls' project description, the developed tiles weigh approximately 200 grams each, compared with early prototypes that weighed more than one kilogram. The modular design also allows individual components to be repaired or replaced without discarding an entire shelter.Natural features such as tree hollows, fallen logs and rocky crevices provide essential places for animals to rest, nest, hide from predators and raise their young. However, land clearing, development and habitat degradation are reducing the availability of these refuges.Tree hollows are particularly important for many native species, but they can take hundreds of years to form naturally. When mature trees disappear, the animals that depend on their hollows can lose essential shelter long before replacement habitats develop.Bush Cradle offers a potential way to bridge this gap by allowing conservationists to construct artificial refuges suited to particular species and landscapes. Its adaptable components provide an alternative to conventional nest boxes, which are often designed for a specific purpose.The system is intended to accommodate different native Australian animals by allowing shelters to be tailored to their habitat requirements.: These spotted, nocturnal marsupials use dens and other sheltered spaces. Bush Cradle can be configured to mimic hollow logs and ground refuges, with entrances and chambers adapted to their needs.: These tree-dwelling marsupials need protected places to rest. A Bush Cradle prototype installed in a tree was reportedly occupied by wild ringtail possums overnight.: Earls has identified potential applications for pygmy possums, reptiles, endangered skinks and microbats. Different configurations could accommodate their varying entrance sizes and shelter requirements.Trail-camera footage reportedly recorded ringtail possums using a Bush Cradle prototype installed in a tree overnight. The observation provided an early indication that the structure could serve as a usable refuge beyond the design studio.However, a single observation cannot establish whether the shelters improve long-term survival, breeding success or population recovery. Further monitoring would be needed to determine how consistently different species use the structures and how well they perform under varying weather conditions.Earls created Bush Cradle as his final-year industrial design project at Monash University in Australia. His work combines ecological research, digital modelling, 3D printing and material experimentation to explore how design could help address habitat loss.An internship at Reef Design Lab helped him explore how digital fabrication and casting could be combined to produce habitat structures. Earls now works full-time at the organisation, continuing to investigate how design can support ecosystems.Bush Cradle received a Best in Class Award in the Next Gen category at the 2026 Australian Good Design Awards, according to Monash University. The recognition highlighted the project's approach to combining industrial design with wildlife conservation.Earls aims to establish a network of conservationists who can use Bush Cradle to create customised wildlife refuges in Australia and potentially elsewhere. The project has also attracted interest for possible use in restoring habitat for endangered skinks and microbats in mining-affected areas of northern Queensland.The long-term ambition is to make artificial habitat creation more accessible, allowing conservationists to respond to the requirements of different species rather than relying on a single shelter design.
Article Summary: Australian designer Xavier Earls has developed a modular wildlife habitat system made from hempcrete tiles. The system is designed to help conservationists create customised refuges for native animals facing habitat loss. Its four interlocking tile designs can be assembled into different configurations, including tree hollows and ground dens, with entrances tailored to individual species.

Article Title: In 2026, a deep-sea robot filmed a black swallower off Trinidad and Tobago with a distended belly after it gulped prey up to 10 times its weight
Article Text:
AI Representation: A deep-sea robot filmed a black swallower off Trinidad and Tobago with a see-through bell. Image credits: Chatgpt

ROV SuBastian filmed the black swallower during the June 29 to July 28, 2026 expedition

Falkor (too)

The fish can swallow prey up to ten times its own weight

Its distended stomach revealed an unusual adaptation

Cold seeps support specialized communities, including tube worms, in chemically rich environments on the seafloor. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The deep ocean is home to animals with unusual ways of finding and consuming food. Some predators have evolved to swallow prey much larger than themselves, an adaptation that can be especially useful where meals are difficult to find. During a deep-sea expedition off Trinidad and Tobago in 2026, researchers captured footage of a black swallower with a remarkably distended stomach after consuming a large meal. The encounter involved the black swallower (Chiasmodon niger), a deep-sea fish known for swallowing prey far larger than itself. The video recording was made as part of a survey led by Trinidadian marine biologist Diva Amon.The sighting took place during the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s Deep Wonders of Trinidad and Tobago expedition, which ran from June 29 to July 28, 2026, as the institute’s cruise page lists. The month-long survey was conducted aboard the research vessel, with researchers using the remotely operated vehicle SuBastian to explore underwater habitats. The Schmidt Ocean Institute describes the expedition as the first locally led and most comprehensive deep-sea survey of Trinidad and Tobago’s surrounding waters, and its announcement confirms that the team captured footage of a black swallower with a distended stomach after it had eaten a meal much larger than itself.The black swallower is a small deep-sea predator with an unusual feeding strategy. Its large mouth, elongated lower jaw and expandable stomach allow it to engulf fish much larger than itself. The Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution’s black swallower profile explains that the species can swallow prey weighing up to ten times its own mass. Its backward-pointing, interlocking teeth help hold prey in place and prevent it from escaping once swallowed.This feeding behavior is especially advantageous in the deep sea, where food may be scarce and finding food sources might be random. Eating much in a single hunt gives the fish much energy without having to hunt for food continuously.What stood out in the video was the extreme swelling of the fish’s abdomen. The fish’s stomach had swollen to hold a meal much larger than it could normally carry. The black swallower was one of many observations made during the survey. The team documented 25 cold seeps and the institute’s announcement says the mapping covered about 13% of Trinidad and Tobago’s marine territory.Cold seeps are areas where there is emission of methane and other substances from the seabed, providing a habitat for organisms that have adapted to the chemically rich environment. Such records helped scientists establish the distribution of deep-sea organisms and pinpoint areas that might require further investigation. The project showed the value of local scientists using ROVs, seafloor mapping and specimen collection in marine research.
Article Summary: The black swallower (Chiasmodon niger) is a small deep-sea predator with an unusual feeding strategy. Its large mouth, elongated lower jaw and expandable stomach allow it to engulf fish much larger than itself. The sighting took place during the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s Deep Wonders of Trinidad and Tobago expedition in 2026.

Article Title: A Buckinghamshire wildlife garden redesigned around an unheated natural swimming pond that attracts frogs, bats, and dragonflies
Article Text:
Image: Julie Skelton

A wildlife and wellbeing brief, how Rachel Platt connected a Buckinghamshire garden to the countryside

Inside the unheated natural swimming pool, a plant-free swim zone and a planted regeneration zone

Frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds, all the wildlife that has moved into the garden's ponds

The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value (Image: Julie Skelton)

How drainage reshaped the plan and kept old favourites

Edible hedgerow, uncut winter meadow, and autumn colour; planting that completes the wildlife garden

A place where the daily swim could begin at the back door, surrounded by dragonflies and flowering plants, even in winter, was the dream of two owners in south Buckinghamshire, who work in the veterinary sector and wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt answered with an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, bats, dragonflies, and more. Read on to discover how the design works, which plants and features support wildlife, what changed along the way, and how the owners describe their transformed outdoor sanctuary. The garden shows how thoughtful landscaping can combine everyday enjoyment with a thriving habitat, creating a peaceful retreat that evolves with the seasons.According to Homes and Gardens, which featured the project in an article by Rachel Bull, the owners both work in the veterinary sector and dreamed of a garden linked to the rolling fields and hedgerows around them. Their brief asked for a biodiverse landscape that would support wildlife while also providing space to swim, grow food, entertain, and spend more time outdoors. Rachel Platt Garden Design responded with a layout that deliberately changes character as it moves away from the house: stronger geometry near the building gives way to softer curves, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an experimental edible hedgerow toward the fields beyond.Before the redesign, the owners regularly drove elsewhere to swim in rivers and spent relatively little time in their own garden, so the new design was meant to bring that experience home.At the heart of the garden sits an unheated natural swimming pool, created as both a wildlife habitat and a place for the owners to reconnect with nature, Homes and Gardens reports. Designer Rachel Platt developed it in collaboration with Ellicar Natural Pools. The pool is divided into a swim zone, kept clear of plants and wildlife, and a regeneration zone planted with a range of aquatic species that filter the water naturally, a process the article calls hydrobotanical filtration. Around the shoreline, water mint, water forget-me-nots, native flag irises, marsh marigolds, ragged robin, and purple loosestrife add colour, seasonal structure, and fragrance, flowering from March to September and attracting pollinators and moths. Deeper-growing aquatics such as common water plantain and arrowhead offer late summer flowers and seedheads, and give emerging dragonflies stems to climb while they unfurl their wings.The wildlife has arrived in force. Homes and Gardens reports that dragonflies and bats were already drawn to the pool, with planting softening its edges and tying it into the wider ecosystem. The owners told Homes and Gardens that frogs, toads, and newts breed in all the ponds, as do several dragonfly species, and that they have even spotted a water snake. Birds also visit, using a beach area, a feature not found in conventional ponds, to enter the water and bathe safely. The owners described the pond as a total escape through every season, and said the garden has become a haven where they feel miles away from everything. For anyone planning a wildlife garden, the lesson is that a single well-planned water feature can support amphibians, insects, mammals, and birds at the same time.The pool was not always meant to be round. According to Homes and Gardens, the original concept was a formal linear pond positioned to reflect a mature birch tree visible through large French doors off the open-plan kitchen and living space. Existing drainage and a suspected utility service running across the garden forced a rethink, and the design became a circular pool. Sustainability and sentiment guided other decisions too. The existing terrace and two ponds were kept for their environmental value and the wildlife they support, and much of the existing planting was saved or relocated, including the owners' fig tree, lily of the valley, raspberries, and rhubarb. Reusing what already works reduces waste and preserves habitat, while keeping familiar plants gives the new garden a sense of continuity with the owners' past.Beyond the pool, an edible hedge links the garden to the landscape, Homes and Gardens says, combining common hazel, hawthorn, blackberry, black chokeberry, damson, pear, and serviceberry to provide structure, blossom, fruit, and habitat. It leads gradually into the meadow, which the owners deliberately leave uncut over winter so that insects, birds, and small mammals can feed on seeds and find a place to overwinter. Autumn colour was also requested, so ornamental grasses such as Miscanthus 'Beth Chatto' and perennials such as Ceratostigma plumbaginoides and white gaura carry warm tones, while burning bush adds bright red. A kitchen garden, grapevine pergola, firepit, and outdoor shower complete the picture. Summing up the transformation, the owners told Homes and Gardens, "We really have our own little Eden," and called the redesign the best decision they have ever made.
Article Summary: Two owners in Buckinghamshire wanted a garden connected to the surrounding fields. Garden designer Rachel Platt designed an unheated natural swimming pool, a sweeping chalk meadow, and an edible hedgerow. The result attracts frogs, toads, newts, dragonflies, bats, and birds.

Article Title: In 2024, a New Jersey dissertation reported on asphalt that heats itself; conductive road strips maintained a snow-free surface at about 6 watts per square foot
Article Text:
AI Representation: New Jersey researchers tested self-heating asphalt embedded with conductive strips. Image credits: Chatgpt

The CREATES test strips in Glassboro

What the Transportation Research Record paper found about power

Full-Scale Evaluation of

Electrically Conductive Asphalt

Pavements for Deicing Applications

Transportation Research Record

A loaded test truck applies repeated traffic loading at an asphalt pavement test track. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The 6 watts per square foot figure in Marath’s 2024 dissertation

Development of Electrically Conductive Asphalt Pavements for Deicing Applications in Cold Regions

Operating costs of $2,280 per hour and the airfield use case

Clearing snow from pavement usually means either removing it by force or dissolving it with chemicals. Plows scrape the road surface, while salt changes how water freezes and then drains into soil and water systems. Both methods require labor, equipment and repeated passes through a storm. A third method uses the road itself as the heating element. Because asphalt is not a good conductor of electricity, engineers must add conductive materials and electrodes to the asphalt layers to heat it with current. The current warms the asphalt enough to melt snow, and the technology has been tested at Rowan University’s accelerated pavement testing facility in southern New Jersey.The research comes from the Center for Research and Education in Advanced Transportation Engineering Systems (CREATES), part of Rowan University’s Henry M. Rowan College of Engineering. The center is housed at the South Jersey Technology Park on Rowan University’s West Campus in New Jersey. The team worked with the U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center’s Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory.ASME reports that the conductive mixture contains 30% graphite and 1% carbon fiber by volume of asphalt binder. In a study published in Transportation Research Record , researchers from Rowan University reported that their laboratory-prepared conductive asphalt mixtures achieved an electrical resistivity of 1 to 2 ohm-meters (Ω·m), averaging 1.21 Ω·m.The first one was the control strip without any electrodes. The second design used a 0.4-inch conductive layer with steel electrodes spaced 6 and 12 inches apart. The third used a 1-inch conductive layer with electrodes spaced 12 inches apart in one section and 6 inches apart in the other. The New Jersey field tests were conducted during the winters of 2021 and 2022, according to Rowan University’s announcement.Rowan announced the full-scale results in November 2023, after the paper appeared in Transportation Research Record that year. The paper,, covered the winters of 2021 and 2022. Rowan University announced the full-scale test results on November 29, 2023. The research paper appeared in, volume 2679, issue 1, in January 2025. The paper says the team built three 30-by-15-foot full-scale strips at Rowan University’s Accelerated Pavement Testing Facility: one control lane and two electrically conductive sections.Strip II used an asphalt binder with conductive fibers, while strip III used a modified high-performance thin overlay with graphite and carbon fibers; strip III also let the researchers compare 12-inch and 6-inch electrode spacing under the same 24V AC setup. ASME reported that strip two consumed about three times more power than strip three, but the paper’s abstract gives 19.75 watts per square foot for strip two against 4.92 for strip three, which is nearly four times as much.The lowest-power result appears in a doctoral dissertation by Ashith Marath,, approved at Rowan on September 26, 2024. The abstract of the dissertation says the conductive asphalt test strips could maintain a snow-free pavement surface with a thermal power output as low as 6 watts per square foot (65 watts per square meter) under winter conditions in New Jersey. The abstract of Marath’s laboratory study says mixtures with 30% graphite had electrical resistivity similar to those with 15% graphite and 2% carbon fiber. Accelerated truck loading using a Heavy Vehicle Simulator found that the heated strips worked about as well as regular asphalt.Power demand determines the running cost, so the low-power finding matters here. ASME’s estimate of $2,280 an hour for a million square feet at $0.19 per kilowatt-hour works out to about 12 watts per square foot, which is double the dissertation’s 6 watts and well above the 4.92 watts per square foot reported for the third strip, so the figures are not directly comparable. Heating cannot fully offset the cost of manual snow and ice removal, which is why Yusuf Mehta, the center’s director, said the system is designed mainly for short stretches such as airports and bridges, where safety and uninterrupted operation justify the expense. The system was also being tested in Alaska during fall 2023 and winter 2024. Life expectancy becomes another reason to use heated pavements. Plows set at the wrong height can damage the asphalt and peel off the sealant, while deicing salts accelerate freeze-thaw damage and shorten the pavement’s life.
Article Summary: Asphalt is not a good conductor of electricity, engineers must add conductive materials and electrodes to the asphalt layers to heat it with current. The current warms the asphalt enough to melt snow, and the technology has been tested at Rowan University’s accelerated pavement testing facility in southern New Jersey.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.

This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Spotify moves to keep AI-generated ‘Slop’ and spam out of user recommendations
Article Text:
How Spotify identifies spam

Spotify has escalated its fight against synthetic audio, announcing that it has pulled more than 50 million AI-generated “slop” and spam tracks out of its algorithmic recommendations this year to safeguard listeners' discovery feeds and ensure human artistry takes center stage. The recommendation ‘update’ comes on top of the permanent removal of more than 75 million spam tracks that were deleted outright for repeated or severe violations of platform rules. According to the company, the sweeping crackdown follows internal reviews conducted earlier this year, where Spotify tracked which songs listeners actively skipped, ignored or flagged. The data exposed a consistent pattern: the vast majority of discarded music was low-quality AI-generated filler or manipulative spam.As standalone AI detection tools have inherent limitations that will become more pronounced as generative models advance, Spotify said it uses a multi-layered verification system rather than relying on a single signal. The platform combines several behavioural and technical checkpoints, including tracking real-time skip patterns, negative user feedback and low engagement.It also monitors unusual mass drops, duplicate song submissions and artificially shortened track lengths.Spotify also hunts down automated SEO manipulation techniques and organised spam playlist syndicates. There are also cross-referencing findings against several independent AI detection utilities.Spotify outlined several artist-protection tools deployed over the past year to establish transparency and build trust across its catalog. One of them is AI Credits which was launched in April. The feature allows creators to log exactly which production roles or instruments utilised artificial intelligence (AI). With artists now filing tens of thousands of AI disclosures daily, listeners can view the details under “Song Credits” in the mobile “Now Playing” interface.More than 300,000 artists, who collectively represent over 99% of search queries on the service, are now verified with a badge confirming an authentic person is behind the catalog. Over 70% of those verified are independent artists, the company said.“As AI makes music more abundant, we believe listeners will value human artistry even more. Our job is to make Spotify the place they find it.”Over the past six months, Spotify rolled out targeted upgrades to its recommendation algorithms and editorial standards to filter out synthetic filler and elevate authentic musicians.
Article Summary: Spotify has pulled more than 50 million AI-generated “slop” and spam tracks out of its algorithmic recommendations this year. The recommendation ‘update’ comes on top of the permanent removal of more than 75 million spam tracks that were deleted outright.

Article Title: Microsoft says AI agents inside companies can’t be trusted, wants ‘Guardian Agents’ to watch their moves
Article Text:
Guarding the companies with ‘Guardian Agents’

At a time when there is a growing wave of publicly disclosed safety incidents highlighting the sheer power and potential hazards of modern artificial intelligence (AI) and AI agents, cybersecurity experts are sounding the alarm on an overlooked vulnerability: the autonomous software agents operating inside corporate networks. While the broader tech industry has remained fixated on external cybercriminals weaponizing models, companies have quietly deployed thousands of internal agents to handle everyday business processes. Microsoft says that since these agents were implemented internally, organisations have largely treated them with implicit trust, there is a need for ‘Guardian Agents’ to make matters more secure.When optimised purely to attain targets, AI models are prone to reward hacking – cutting corners or finding unintended loopholes that violate organisational judgment and unwritten business norms. And as the global race for innovation accelerates, these containment challenges will only multiply as underlying models become more capable.To prevent agentic insiders from triggering enterprise disruptions, security professionals argue that oversight must be continuous, real-time and pre-emptive.An autonomous agent combines a frontier model, an orchestration harness, an assigned action space of tools, and an execution runtime.Defending this footprint requires security controls spanning identity, permissions, data layers, endpoints, networks and cloud runtimes. Guardian Agents are an established industry mechanism where dedicated supervisory models monitor and moderate every planned action of every operational agent 24/7, before that action is actually executed.First announced by Microsoft in July to help cyber defenders outpace AI-driven attacks originating outside corporate walls, Project Perception is now being directed inward to oversee and govern internal agentic insiders. Built to impose deterministic controls on non-deterministic artificial intelligence, the platform uses a multi-layered cyber architecture.It gathers telemetry across identity, data, endpoints, network, and runtime environments to identify untracked agents in the enterprise; evaluates incoming telemetry in real time to calculate the exact risk profile of what an agent is trying to accomplish and then uses collaborative teams of Guardian, “green,” and “blue” agents to supervise actions around the clock.By pairing algorithmic speed with human oversight, security practitioners gain complete traceability to investigate what happened, analyze why a risk surfaced, and exercise human judgment to calibrate security rules.
Article Summary: Microsoft says that since these agents were implemented internally, organisations have largely treated them with implicit trust. There is a need for ‘Guardian Agents’ to make matters more secure. When optimised purely to attain targets, AI models are prone to reward hacking – cutting corners or finding unintended loopholes.

Article Title: Microsoft says AI agents should start with zero access, unveils new security controls
Article Text:
Why agents are an insider risk

What Microsoft is adding

Microsoft has announced a set of new security tools aimed at treating AI agents as a new kind of insider risk, with controls designed to limit what each agent can access and to tighten those limits automatically if its behaviour changes. The announcement was made in a blog post by Nadim Abdo, corporate vice president of identity and network access at Microsoft. It extends Project Perception, Microsoft’s agentic security system introduced earlier this year, to cover the agents that companies are deploying across their operations.Abdo said agents are quickly becoming part of how work gets done, from writing code and analysing revenue to processing expenses. To be useful, they often need access to company data, applications and tools, and that access creates insider risk.He stressed that this doesn’t mean agents are inherently malicious. They can make mistakes, be manipulated or be compromised, he said, and an agent that behaves as intended at the start of a task can act differently as its context changes. They can also run continuously at machine speed and scale.Abdo cited remarks by Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, who has argued that security controls must sit outside the AI model, where it can’t bypass or tamper with them.“The most trustworthy agentic system will not be the one with the model we trust most,” Nadella said. “It will be the one designed that enables us to trust the model least.”The company framed its approach around four tasks: know which agents exist, contain what they can do, protect the data and systems in their path, and adapt protection as risk changes. The main new features include:* Wider agent discovery. Microsoft is adding 35 types of local agents, bringing the total supported to 60, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot. Companies can bring them into one registry to see who owns them and what they are doing.* Agent identities. Microsoft Entra Agent ID will add identity types for more agent patterns, including local and previously unknown agents found by security sensors. This is meant to let companies tell what a person did apart from what an agent did on that person’s behalf.* Dynamic Permissions. Agents would start with no authority and receive only what an approved task needs, for only as long as it takes. Organisation-wide policy sets the outer limit, and higher-impact actions can require verified human approval.* Dynamic Agent Risk. A continuously updated risk assessment combining signals from identity, data, endpoints, cloud, network, runtime and the agent’s own activity. It considers whether an agent’s actions are drifting from the intent of its user or organisation.* Dynamic Conditional Access. An extension of Entra Conditional Access for agents. When risk rises, policy can respond in steps: reduce permissions, allow reads but block writes, narrow the resources an agent can reach, require human approval, or isolate the agent and stop it.* Guardian Agents and Playbooks. A team of agents inside Project Perception that investigates why risk changed and recommends or applies containment. People set policy, approval limits and delegation rules.* Model-level evidence. Microsoft plans to feed signals such as chain-of-thought into its risk scoring to spot when an agent’s plans diverge from its task. It said security decisions must remain independent of the model.* Sandboxed runtime. Sandboxes such as Microsoft Execution Container give agents policy-controlled access to resources, so a compromised agent cannot switch off the controls watching it.Abdo illustrated the approach with an expense-approval agent that can read submissions, check policy and approve routine reimbursements, but does not inherit all of its sponsoring employee’s access. If it hits a prompt injection in an outside document or attempts an unrelated action, its risk score rises. Policy could then keep read access, remove the ability to approve or write, block sensitive resources and require provable human approval. If the risk keeps climbing, the system could isolate or stop the agent.Terrell Cox, Microsoft’s corporate vice president and deputy chief information security officer for customer security, said the company is already operating with hundreds of thousands of agents. “Agents will only be adopted at scale if they can be trusted at scale,” he said, adding that Microsoft’s experience as “Customer Zero” informs the new tools.Abdo wrote that the goal is not to make every model perfectly predictable but to build systems that remain secure even when the model is not. “You should not have to choose between innovation and safety,” he said.
Article Summary: Microsoft is adding 35 types of local agents, bringing the total supported to 60. Sandboxes give agents policy-controlled access to resources. Microsoft plans to feed signals such as chain-of-thought into its risk scoring to spot when an agent’s plans diverge from its task.

Article Title: Users claims Meta smartglasses recording them in 'Sleep Mode', say have 'forgotten' the magic words to alert
Article Text:
Meta Ray-Ban Smart Glasses

Users claim unprompted lights and saved transcripts

Other owners quickly echoed the experience:

Meta says the ‘glitch has been fixed’

Privacy alarms are sounding once again for Meta’s smart glasses. Some wearers of Meta’s smart glasses are claiming that the connected eyewear has been recording private conversations and saving transcripts even while the hardware is supposed to be in “sleep mode” – all without hearing the required wake word. Citing three separate Reddit discussion threads, New York Post reports that multiple customers claimed that several iterations of the tech-enabled frames, which allow hands-free communication, audio playback, and video capture, have activated unexpectedly and captured ambient speech without user consent.The complaints center on the eyewear’s voice-trigger mechanism. Normally, wearers must say the prompt phrase “Hey Meta” to wake the glasses and engage the onboard assistant. However, owners say the devices have started bypassing that safeguard altogether following a recent firmware update.One wearer reported documenting the unprompted behaviour across three different pairs of Ray-Ban Meta glasses, covering both second- and third-generation units.“I have observed the same behavior on THREE different pairs of Ray-Ban Meta glasses, including 2nd- and 3rd-generation models. Meta AI does not respond to me, and I never intentionally activated it.I have noticed the white notification light activating while I am speaking normally,” the user wrote, explaining that the glasses began recording conversations with a friend without being prompted.The user added that the companion Meta AI application went so far as to store both audio recordings and written transcripts of those private discussions directly inside their conversation history logs. The owner noted they are preparing to pursue a class-action lawsuit if evidence shows the glitch is widespread.One user reported that resetting the hardware did not solve the problem: “I could see the LED light up in instances where I didn’t invoke Hey Meta.”A second owner noted silent activations: “Mine randomly activates the internal light now without any input from me. It does not make the wake-up noise voice command would the internal light just turns on. Something weird is going on!”Another user confirmed the same pattern on older hardware: “I made a post about the AI turning on during random conversations. It’s not just you. I have gen 2.”When contacted regarding the unprompted activations and phantom recordings, Meta did not explain the technical root cause behind the behaviour, but claimed the glitch has been handled.“This issue has been resolved. People can manage, review and delete voice logs of their interactions with Meta AI via settings at any time,” a Meta company spokesperson told The Post.
Article Summary: Users claim unprompted lights and saved transcripts on Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses. Glasses allow hands-free communication, audio playback, and video capture. Wearers must say the prompt phrase “Hey Meta” to wake the glasses and engage the onboard assistant.

Article Title: From bookings to handwritten notes, Apple's Siri finds a way into Indian apps
Article Text:
Apple's Siri

Getting the best out of Siri

New Delhi: Finding a contract, checking a movie booking or searching handwritten notes no longer necessarily requires opening an app and navigating its menus. Indian developers are integrating their services with Apple ’s upgraded Siri, allowing users to describe what they need and retrieve information or trigger actions through voice commands.In case you were wondering what the fuss over new Siri is, then here’s a quick update: Siri AI is Apple’s upgraded voice assistant, designed to understand conversational requests and use context from what users are viewing. Apple has connected it more closely with apps, allowing developers to make searches, information and actions accessible through Siri. Instead of remembering a fixed command, users can describe what they want or refer to something on screen.District, Glance, Noteshelf, Signeasy and Mood Dial are among the apps adopting these capabilities. Their developers say the change goes beyond earlier Siri integrations, which typically required preset commands or Shortcuts. Users can now make conversational requests and refer to information already displayed on their screens.“Earlier, users had to set up Shortcuts or remember specific phrases to trigger an action,” said Rama Krishna, founder of Fluid Touch, which develops Noteshelf.In Noteshelf, users can ask where they wrote about a Chennai trip, seek an explanation of a diagram or request a summary to be added to an existing note. The integration makes handwritten material accessible through these requests.“Siri also understands what’s on screen, even handwritten notes, so users can ask questions about their notes and add the answers back in,” Krishna said.The same shift is taking place in document management. Signeasy users can retrieve a named contract, check documents awaiting signatures or ask Siri to open an item from the list on screen.“Earlier, Siri could open Signeasy or run a fixed Shortcut, and that was about it,” said Santhosh J, head of mobile at Signeasy.Making these actions available required developers to rethink how their apps function. Apple’s App Intents framework lets them expose individual capabilities—such as searching, retrieving information or creating content—to the operating system. An action previously tied to a particular screen must work independently.“That made us separate what the app does from how it looks,” Santhosh said. A small team built Signeasy’s integration alongside regular releases, with document-related actions accessible through multiple entry points.For consumer apps, that approach creates another route to discovery. District, part of Eternal, lets users search for experiences and retrieve information about dining, movie and event bookings.“Users can discover experiences within District through Siri’s Search in App and Visual Intelligence,” said Adarsh Singh, software development engineer at District.The company exposed its search capabilities and booking data through App Intents. “It also shifted our approach towards making District’s experiences accessible beyond the app itself,” Singh said.Glance is using Siri to deliver shopping recommendations based on preferences including style, fit, budget and favourite brands. Users can see recommendations in Siri’s response or continue browsing in Glance.“The integration took more than 10 weeks of coordinated effort between Glance’s product and technology teams and Apple’s WWDR India team,” said Arvind Jayaprakash, senior vice-president, technology, Glance.However, discovery does not extend to completing a purchase. “Glance helps users discover products that match their preferences, but it doesn’t complete purchases on their behalf,” Jayaprakash said. Users are directed to merchants to review products and pay.For Mood Dial, a music app for Apple Music subscribers, conversational requests replace the need to remember a station’s exact name.“Now you can just say how you feel,” said founder Mohit Nandwani. A request for music suited to a quiet, rainy night can select an existing station or initiate the creation of another.The integration also required a less obvious adjustment: reducing Siri’s spoken responses. “I took the talking out,” Nandwani said, explaining that speech after playback begins pauses the music. Clear requests therefore start playback silently; ambiguous ones prompt clarification.Whether these interactions generate additional business remains unclear. District reported 1,897 successful Visual Intelligence fetches, 329 Search in App queries and 287 booking lookups. It did not specify the measurement period or unique-user count. These are interactions, not completed bookings. Glance, Noteshelf and Signeasy have not shared usage figures.Availability also varies. Most developers described English support on compatible Apple Intelligence devices, with newer capabilities tied to iOS 27. Older, fixed Siri commands can remain available separately. District said its Visual Search supports Hindi and English.Data handling differs by action. Noteshelf says it uses on-device processing and makes notebook information searchable through Spotlight. Signeasy says its contract summaries use Apple’s on-device Foundation Models, keeping document content on the phone.Mood Dial says matching a request to an existing station happens locally. Creating a new station sends the user’s sentence to its server under an anonymous identifier, with confirmation required before creation. Health data is excluded from Siri requests.Consequential actions retain additional steps. Signeasy requires signing within the app and manual review before sending through Mail; Glance leaves checkout to merchants. Developers have opened new routes into their services, but have yet to demonstrate whether users will regularly choose them over tapping through an app. Can the new and improved Siri AI become a daily habit for users? If app developers continue integrating it and expand on its use cases, then perhaps that's a possibility.
Article Summary: Indian developers are integrating their services with Apple ’s upgraded Siri. Users can describe what they need and retrieve information or trigger actions through voice commands. District, Glance, Noteshelf, Signeasy and Mood Dial are among the apps adopting these capabilities.

Article Title: This US AI lab offers free plumbing, electrical work and other tasks in three cities but there is a catch: Workers will wear sensors that…
Article Text:
Representative image

‘Web-scraped data no longer enough’

‘Capturing unpredictable real-world work’

An AI laboratory specialising in real-world data collection is offering homeowners free home repairs and maintenance services across three major US cities. However, the program comes with a specific condition: the technicians sent to do the job will wear sensors to record their movements to collect data that will be used to train the next generation of AI-powered robots. The startup, called HUMXN, announced that it will fully subsidise essential trade services, including plumbing, electrical work, HVAC repairs, air-duct cleaning and carpet cleaning.As per a report by Tom’s Hardware, under the arrangement, residents who need repairs can receive qualified services at no financial cost. In exchange, they must agree to allow trade professionals outfitted with “wearable capture technology” into their homes to record how they perform complex, physical tasks on-site.The push into home comes as tech companies have reportedly understood that digital text, web photos and online video clips are insufficient for teaching physical machines how to operate in everyday environments.“The next generation of AI is going to need more than text and images from the internet. Robots need to understand how skilled people interact with the physical world. Home-service technicians perform millions of highly technical tasks every day.We are creating a way for homeowners and service companies to benefit financially from the value of that expertise,” said HUMXN founder Thomas Unise.Unise noted that while millions of trade specialists execute sophisticated mechanical operations daily, virtually none of that practical knowledge is cataloged in digital formats that machine-learning models can process.“We want to build the infrastructure that connects that knowledge with the companies building the next generation of intelligent machines while making sure the people creating the value participate in the economics,” Unise added.According to HUMXN, attempting to recreate the natural, instinctive motions of skilled laborers inside artificial laboratory environments is difficult. By sending technicians into actual residences, the company can record authentic workflows across diverse housing layouts, varied equipment types, unique structural problems, individual technician styles and different environmental conditions.The recorded sensor telemetry will provide AI models with detailed, step-by-step insight into how experienced technicians solve problems in real time. This includes inspecting physical fixtures and diagnosing malfunctions; testing active home systems; selecting the proper tools for specific scenarios; adapting to changing physical conditions on the job, and verifying that a repair has been completed successfully and safely.The company is rolling out the initiative across three select markets chosen to capture operational data across sharply different regional climates: Chicago, Minneapolis and Miami. Residents living in those three metropolitan areas can verify their eligibility by visiting the official HUMXN Free Home Service webpage.
Article Summary: HUMXN is offering free home repairs and maintenance services across three major US cities. In exchange, technicians will wear sensors to record their movements to collect data that will be used to train the next generation of AI-powered robots. The company is rolling out the initiative across three select markets chosen to capture operational data across sharply different regional climates.
